title: New patient: outside records pending
description: Adversarial fixture. LVEF is patient-reported and hedged, no ECG, no NYHA class, heart-failure type never stated, AF history uncertain, beta-blocker adherence poor, unnamed diuretic, ivabradine only mentioned as a possibility.
synthetic_notice: Entirely fictional. Not derived from any real patient or encounter.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Hi Mrs. Lindqvist, I'm Dr. Reyes. I understand you were in the hospital in Tucson this spring for your heart.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Yes, in April. The doctor there said my heart was pumping at like twenty percent. Or maybe twenty-five, I don't remember exactly.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: We don't have that echo report yet. We'll request the records from Tucson.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: How is your breathing day to day?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: I get short of breath walking out to the mailbox. And I'm tired all the time.

segments.speaker: staff
segments.text: Blood pressure 94 over 58. Pulse felt a little irregular, I counted about 88.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Has anyone ever told you that you have atrial fibrillation?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: I think they said something about that in the hospital, but I'm not sure. They gave me a lot of papers.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: What medications are you taking right now?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: The carvedilol, I think it's the 12.5. But I've been skipping the night one because it makes me so tired.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: And a water pill. I don't remember the name. It's in my bag somewhere.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: That's okay, we'll go through the bottles before you leave.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Before we change anything, I want an ECG and those outside records. If your rhythm is regular and your heart rate stays up once you're taking the carvedilol consistently, ivabradine might be something to consider down the road.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Okay. Whatever you think is best.
